articles.title: Ferrari say team has ‘made its choices’ and there’s no vacancy for Christian Horner
articles.summary: Marque reaffirms commitment to Fred Vasseur. Horner had expressed interest in joining Ferrari. Ferrari have reaffirmed their backing for team principal Fred Vasseur in an effort to end speculation that Christian Horner was being considered as a potential replacement for the Frenchman.
body: Horner gave an interview in the Times last week in which he stated that leading Ferrari would be his “dream” job and the only one he would consider without having part-ownership of the team. His comments provoked debate that he could replace Vasseur, given the Scuderia’s underperformance this season.

On Tuesday, Ferrari took the unusual step of holding an unscheduled media call in an effort to close down the chatter with the team’s chief communication officer, Maria Conti, speaking on behalf of the chair, John Elkann and the chief executive officer, Benedetto Vigna.
“Ferrari’s position is clear, has not changed, and Ferrari has made its choices already. We have confidence, full confidence, in Fred Vasseur and in his team, and we continue to do so,” she said.
“Everybody, they are still creating a lot of different stories around Fred and this is not useful. We do not intend to fuel speculation or comment on assumptions coming from outside the company.”

Horner gave an interview in the Times last week in which he stated that leading Ferrari would be his “dream” job and the only one he would consider without having part-ownership of the team.
“Ferrari’s position is clear, has not changed, and Ferrari has made its choices already.
We have confidence, full confidence, in Fred Vasseur and in his team, and we continue to do so,” she said.

articles.title: Manchester City found guilty on all Premier League charges over rule breaches
articles.summary: ‘Sham’ contracts helped inflate revenues by £900m. Commission finds club guilty over nine-season period. Manchester City have been found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules over a nine-season period, the league has announced.
body: Manchester City breached Premier League financial rules by creating “sham” contracts to help inflate revenue and reduce costs by more than £900m over a nine-year period, an independent commission found.

The league announced on Tuesday that City had been found guilty on all charges related to serious breaches of its financial rules between seasons 2009-10 and 2017-18. It said a sanction would be addressed in a further hearing with the commission.

City created a number of commercial deals with sponsors that were part of a scheme to disguise where the funding was coming from, the commission concluded. Companies were required to pay only a portion of the stipulated fees, with the remainder funded by the Abu Dhabi United Group Investment + Development Ltd (Adug), which owned the club.

articles.summary: The Premier League confirms that Manchester City have been found guilty of all charges related to breaches of Premier League financial rules between 2009-10 and 2017-18.
body: An independent Commission found that during that time period, the club arranged "sham contracts" with a number of its commercial partners, as well as "relying on sham agreements to artificially inflate the club's revenues and reduce its costs".
The statement also said that City were guilty of the majority of charges in relation to its failure to co-operate.

The Premier League published a redacted version of the commission's report, which said the charges "concerned well over 100 alleged individual breaches of Premier League Rules across four broad charge categories".
They also found the club guilty of all charges except one relating to non-cooperation with the Premier League investigation.

articles.title: How important is a fast start for teams chasing the Premier League title?
articles.summary: Manchester City have kicked off the campaign with five victories in a row but the title race is a marathon not a sprint. By Opta Analyst. The first international window gives us time to take stock and make sense of what has happened in the early weeks of the Premier League season.
body: Of course, we do not yet know the punishment they may face for breaking the Premier League’s financial fair play rules so, for the purposes of this article, we will put that matter to the side.

Enzo Maresca’s side became the 15th different team to win their opening five games of a Premier League season, and it’s the fourth occasion City have managed it. They have only won the title in one of the three previous seasons, though. They won the league in 2023-24, but failed to capitalise on their five early wins in 2015-16 and 2016-17.

That follows a wider trend across the league. Only four of the 14 teams that have won their first five matches of the season have gone on to win the title (29%): Manchester City in 2023-24, Liverpool in 2019-20, and Chelsea in 2009-10 and 2005-06.

Perhaps most importantly, all four teams went on to add to their winning streak to start those seasons. Chelsea in 2009-10 and Manchester City in 2023-24 extended their run by another game (six wins); Liverpool started with eight wins in 2019-20; and Chelsea (nine wins in 2005-06) went on the longest winning run to start a Premier League season.
points: Manchester City have kicked off the campaign with five victories in a row but the title race is a marathon not a sprint.
The first international window gives us time to take stock and make sense of what has happened in the early weeks of the Premier League season.

body: Molango said Palmer's recent withdrawal from the England squad highlighted a match calendar that is unsustainable and has become the "survival of the fittest".
Five players – Palmer, Marcus Rashford, Declan Rice, Kobbie Mainoo and Tino Livramento, external - pulled out of Thomas Tuchel's squad ahead of the latest international window.

"When England see five players who need to withdraw when the single most proud moment a player has is to be called up for the national team, you just ask yourself, what's wrong about the industry?" Molango said at the Fifpro performance summit in London.
"You see people like Cole Palmer, someone who would have played four consecutive summers in a row had he gone to the World Cup, and you wonder why is he missing?

articles.summary: There have been pretty rampant rumors that the Arizona Cardinals could trade former first-round pick of the Arizona Cardinals, Marvin Harrison Jr. and the Las Vegas Raiders are among the teams that have been most coonected to him.

articles.title: Joe Buck ‘hopeful’ Troy Aikman stays at ESPN
articles.summary: After following Troy Aikman to ESPN, Joe Buck now hopes his longtime NFL broadcast partner follows him in staying at ESPN. Earlier this month, Buck signed a six-year contract extension with ESPN worth more than $100 million to continue as the network’s voice of Monday Night Football.
body: Buck joined Unfiltered with Ricky Bo and Bill Colarulo on Philadelphia 's 97.5 The Fanatic earlier this week to preview the Eagles Monday Night Football matchup with the Chicago Bears. And during the interview, Buck addressed Aikman's uncertain status with ESPN.

"I'm pretty well on record, having begged out of my last years at Fox to follow him to ESPN, where I stand on all that," Buck said, confirming he hopes Aikman reaches a deal with ESPN. "I legitimately love the guy like a brother. We're basically the same age; I'm 57, he's 59. We've both been through divorce. We're both girl dads. 25 years, you're sharing a lot of life together. Forget games and in the booth and all that stuff.

"So, I hope so. I mean, both of us were up. It wasn't like we were doing some national signing day where we walk in arm-in-arm and then sign contracts at the same time. We've always kind of kept that stuff separate. I'm obviously hopeful, to say the least, that something gets done. But that's kind of his world, and ESPN's world, and I've got to kind of mind my own yard in that stuff. I think that's the best way to be."

articles.title: Buttler: McCullum can go 'all in' on Cricket World Cup without Test role
articles.summary: Jos Buttler believes Brendon McCullum's removal as Test coach may have boosted England's World Cup chances, with the New Zealander now "all in" on lifting the trophy next winter.
body: McCullum was relieved of his red-ball duties in July, with Stephen Fleming eventually named as his successor, but remained in charge of a limited-overs set-up that ended the summer with a record of 11 wins and two defeats.
That included ODI series wins over India and Sri Lanka, raising England's stock in a format that has seen them decline since they became world champions in 2019.
Buttler, who captained the team in their ill-fated 2023 title defence, thinks the split coaching model has allowed McCullum to throw all his energy towards next year's tournament in southern Africa.
"He's only got one focus now and that is the white ball," Buttler said on his For the Love of Cricket podcast.

articles.title: How Verstappen can disrupt Antonelli, Russell title fight
articles.summary: The 2026 Formula 1 title race has become a two-horse race between Mercedes duo Kimi Antonelli and George Russell with eight rounds remaining.
body: Antonelli leads Russell by 66 points ahead of this weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia and it will be fascinating to see how the Italian responds following what he called his "worst weekend" of the season last time out in Baku.
Depending on the quality of Mercedes' major upgrade package that will be introduced in Malaysia this week, we could see the Silver Arrows dominate the last third of the season.
However, there's one driver everyone on the grid mentions every weekend when it comes to who could challenge, or who will be a threat - and that's Max Verstappen.

This year is the first season Verstappen has not challenged for the title since 2020, having won four championships in a row from 2021 to 2024 and coming just two points short of an incredible comeback in 2025 to defeat Lando Norris.
